rv.q: Iglesias’s journey from dutiful to dominant is a wonderful showcase of range.
He constructs an intricate yet expansive Cuba-in-miniature where the fate of the country seems to rest on individual relationships.
If only the dialogue and events in the first act were less wooden, the characters more nuanced, and the issues more developed.

cn.t: Machado's era-spanning drama traces four decades of Cuban revolution through one woman's kitchen, delivering spellbinding political intrigue and family scandal that critics find engrossing if occasionally uneven in its ambitious scope.
